title: bug: Unable to connect to LDAP
body: ### Describe the bug When starting from scratch (via Docker Compose) I am unable to initialise Homarr with LDAP as the provider. Whenever I try to log in after setting up the users and groups, I get the following in the logs: ``` 2026-02-18T22:49:12.587Z info: User is trying to log in using LDAP. Connecting to LDAP server... module="ldapAuthorization" userName="admin" 2026-02-18T22:49:12.595Z error: Read more at https://errors.authjs.dev#credentialssignin module="authConfiguration" name="E" type="CredentialsSignin" kind="signIn" code="credentials" at rk (/app/apps/nextjs/.next/server/chunks/_607de06c._.js:404:17922) at process.processTicksAndRejections (node:internal/process/task_queues:103:5) at async rj (/app/apps/nextjs/.next/server/chunks/_607de06c._.js:404:27449) at async rN (/app/apps/nextjs/.next/server/chunks/_607de06c._.js:404:31703) at async d (/app/apps/nextjs/.next/server/chunks/[root-of-the-server]__bd75a333._.js:1:2756) at async rU.do (/app/node_modules/next/dist/compiled/next-server/app-route-turbo.runtime.prod.js:5:20169) at async rU.handle (/app/node_modules/next/dist/compiled/next-server/app-route-turbo.runtime.prod.js:5:24949) at async u (/app/apps/nextjs/.next/server/chunks/[root-of-the-server]__bd75a333._.js:1:6673) at async rU.handleResponse (/app/node_modules/next/dist/compiled/next-server/app-route-turbo.runtime.prod.js:1:101467) at async d (/app/apps/nextjs/.next/server/chunks/[root-of-the-server]__bd75a333._.js:1:7714) ``` The issue is that I can query the LDAP server and get the correct users and groups with `ldapsearch` using the same parameters in the Docker Compose file, so it doesn't seem to be an error with the LDAP server **Docker Compose** LLDAP is just being used as an example LDAP server, but I have the same issues with an Authentik LDAP Outpost ```yaml services: homarr: image: ghcr.io/homarr-labs/homarr:v1.52.0 container_name: homarr restart: unless-stopped ports: - "7575:7575" environment: SECRET_ENCRYPTION_KEY: '18db364d73b613c0729b9131d2d91eee64bebad7b8a9838ab619528a1a8afb69' LOG_LEVEL: "debug" AUTH_PROVIDERS: "ldap" AUTH_LDAP_URI: "ldap://lldap:3890" AUTH_LDAP_BASE: "dc=local" AUTH_LDAP_BIND_DN: "cn=admin,ou=people,dc=local" AUTH_LDAP_BIND_PASSWORD: 'password1234' AUTH_LDAP_SEARCH_SCOPE: "sub" lldap: image: lldap/lldap:stable container_name: lldap restart: unless-stopped ports: - '389:3890' - '17170:17170' environment: LLDAP_JWT_SECRET: 'Udas+80alzzRzx5Npv919EyRwTv9/jrJB33U4CyUE18' LLDAP_KEY_SEED: 'piHx69kLIKE3Uy57bnbeEKVPD2XybLgAv2JxQNIKFFs' LLDAP_LDAP_USER_PASS: 'password1234' LLDAP_LDAP_BASE_DN: 'dc=local' ``` **LDAP Queries** Confirm User Exists ```shell ldapsearch \ -b "dc=local" \ -D "cn=admin,ou=people,dc=local" \ -H "ldap://localhost:389" \ -s base \ -x -w "password1234" \ "(uid=admin)" ``` Confirm Group Membership ```shell ldapsearch \ -b "dc=local" \ -D "cn=admin,ou=people,dc=local" \ -H "ldap://localhost:389" \ -s base \ -x -w "password1234" \ "(memberOf=cn=Homarr,ou=groups,dc=local)" ``` ### Steps to reproduce 1. Create Docker Compose file 2. `docker compose up -d` 3. Log in to LLDAP and create "Homarr" group, and assign `admin` (the default) user 4. Open Homarr at `http://localhost:7575` and begin first setup 5. When asked to sign in, try username `admin` and password `password1234` 6. Receive above error ### Impact Using LDAP as a provider is rendered inoperable ### Additional information Screenshot of error in browser ### Version 1.53.0 ### Installation method Docker Compose ### Browser Chrome

full_comments.body: Can you perform a curl or wget from the Homarr container to check whether the network config works?

wget or curl what? It can access internet content
```shell
04ed853b57a7:/app# curl -sL https://homarr.dev >/dev/null && echo success || echo failure
success
```
and
```shell
04ed853b57a7:/app# wget --spider https://homarr.dev >/dev/null && echo success || echo failure
Connecting to homarr.dev (185.199.110.153:443)
remote file exists
success
```
I know the LDAP port is accessible from the Homarr container, confirmed with bash's `/dev/tcp` feature and if you install the `openldap-clients` package and use `ldapsearch` in the container
```shell
04ed853b57a7:/app# timeout 5 bash -c '</dev/tcp/lldap/3890' && echo success || echo failed
success
```
and

Are you sure that you need to use cn=admin and not uid=admin? 
Thats the only thing I can see in a first glance that is different from the documentation

Yep, changing `AUTH_LDAP_BIND_DN: "cn=admin,ou=people,dc=local"` to `AUTH_LDAP_BIND_DN: "uid=admin,ou=people,dc=local"`  in the Docker Compose file (so it matches the DN from the `ldapsearch` result) does fix this issue with the example LLDAP deployment, and does now allow me to sign in with LDAP user credentials. My fault for not paying close enough attention

The issue now then is that using an Authentik LDAP outpost as the LDAP server, even while ensuring the bind DN is correct, does not work

### What I've Changed

**New Docker Compose**
```yaml
services:
  homarr:
    image: ghcr.io/homarr-labs/homarr:latest
    container_name: homarr
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "7575:7575"
    environment:
      SECRET_ENCRYPTION_KEY: '18db364d73b613c0729b9131d2d91eee64bebad7b8a9838ab619528a1a8afb69'
      LOG_LEVEL: "debug"
      AUTH_PROVIDERS: "ldap"
      AUTH_LDAP_URI: "ldap://172.21.181.207:389" # Changed
      AUTH_LDAP_BASE: "dc=local"
      AUTH_LDAP_BIND_DN: "cn=admin,ou=users,dc=local" # Changed 'ou=people' to 'ou=users'
      AUTH_LDAP_BIND_PASSWORD: 'password1234'
      AUTH_LDAP_USERNAME_ATTRIBUTE: "sAMAccountName"
      AUTH_LDAP_SEARCH_SCOPE: "sub" # Added
      AUTH_LDAP_USERNAME_FILTER_EXTRA_ARG: "objectClass=user" # Added
```
- `172.21.181.207` is the IP address of the Docker host, no longer connecting the containers with a Docker network
- Username attribute changed to `sAMAccountName`, as the `uid` attribute in Authentik is a random string
- `AUTH_LDAP_SEARCH_SCOPE` and `AUTH_LDAP_USERNAME_FILTER_EXTRA_ARG` (explained below)

And to confirm these parameters should work, a `ldapsearch` query within the Homarr container
```shell
38bfe3829742:/app# apk add --no-cache openldap-clients
```

You'll notice that there are two results, because Authentik creates matching groups per user (like most UNIX systems), so this may be the issue? I've tried playing around with the `AUTH_LDAP_SEARCH_SCOPE` and `AUTH_LDAP_USERNAME_FILTER_EXTRA_ARG` env variables in the compose file (e.g. `AUTH_LDAP_USERNAME_FILTER_EXTRA_ARG='objectClass=user'` or `AUTH_LDAP_USERNAME_FILTER_EXTRA_ARG='(objectClass=user')`) to filter the groups out, but it still doesn't work

`# base <dc=local> with scope subtree` seems to use `AUTH_LDAP_SEARCH_SCOPE` of `base`. Can you adjust that?
No change unfortunately, still the same error message as above
